title: Telescoping GPU Sag Brace with Cable Comb
summary: A height-adjustable graphics-card support brace that clips a cable comb onto its post so the PCIe power cable routes cleanly instead of dangling.
coordinate_system: Origin at the center of the base-plate's bottom face. +X runs right, +Y runs toward the back of the case, +Z runs up. Each part below carries its own local origin, stated in its first construction step, positioned relative to this global frame when assembled.

parts.name: Base plate
parts.base_shape: Rectangle 70 x 60, corner radius 4, with a square socket boss cut into the top and four magnet pockets cut into the bottom
construction_steps: Sketch on XY at z=0 (origin = center of bottom face): rectangle 70 x 60 centered on origin, corner radius 4
Extrude 16 in +Z
On the top face (z=16), sketch a square 28 x 28 centered at (0,0)
Pocket cut 10 deep from the top face (z=16 down to z=6)
On the bottom face (z=0), sketch four circles 10 diameter, centers at (25,20), (-25,20), (25,-20), (-25,-20)
Pocket cut 3 deep from the bottom face at each of the four circles (z=0 up to z=3)
Chamfer the top outer edge of the plate 1 x 45 degrees for finish

parts.name: Riser tube
parts.base_shape: Hollow square tube, 27.8 x 27.8 outer, 3 mm wall, corner radius 1
construction_steps: Sketch on XY at z=0 (origin = center of bottom end): square 27.8 x 27.8, centered, corner radius 1
Extrude 70 in +Z
Shell the extrusion inward by 3 (wall thickness), leaving the top and bottom faces open
On the front wall (Y = -13.9 plane), sketch 11 circles 3.3 diameter, centered on the face width (X=0), at Z = 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65
Cut each circle through both the front and back walls (through-hole along +Y)

parts.name: Locking pin
parts.base_shape: T-pin: 3 mm diameter shaft with an 8 mm diameter retaining head
construction_steps: Sketch a circle 3 diameter on XY at z=0, centered on origin
Extrude 20 in +Z (shaft)
On top of the shaft (z=20), sketch a circle 8 diameter centered on origin
Extrude 2 in +Z (head disc)

parts.name: GPU cradle
parts.base_shape: Block 65 x 34 x 18 with a bottom socket for the riser and a top trough for the GPU edge
construction_steps: Sketch on XY at z=0 (origin = center of bottom face): rectangle 65 x 34 centered on origin, corner radius 3
Extrude 18 in +Z
On the bottom face (z=0), sketch a square 28.2 x 28.2 centered at (0,0)
Pocket cut 10 deep from the bottom face (z=0 up to z=10)
On the top face (z=18), sketch a slot 55 x 18.2 centered at (0,0) with 4 mm corner radius
Pocket cut 8 deep from the top face (z=18 down to z=10)
On the socket side wall (Y = -14.1 plane, within the pocket), sketch a circle 3.3 diameter centered at (X=0, Z=5 measured from the part's bottom face)
Cut the circle through both socket side walls (through-hole along Y)

parts.name: Friction pad
parts.base_shape: Flat strip, 55 x 18 x 2, press-fit into the cradle trough
construction_steps: Sketch on XY at z=0 (origin = center of the strip): rectangle 55 x 18 centered on origin, corner radius 2
Extrude 2 in +Z

parts.name: Cable comb
parts.base_shape: Block 40 x 15 x 12 with 6 top slots and two rear snap prongs
construction_steps: Sketch on XY at z=0 (origin = center of back-bottom edge): rectangle 40 x 15 centered on X, from Y=0 to Y=15
Extrude 12 in +Z
On the top face (z=12), sketch a row of 6 rectangles, each 3 x 15, spaced 3 apart, centered as a group on X=0
Pocket cut 6 deep from the top face at each rectangle (z=12 down to z=6)
On the back face (Y=0 plane), sketch two rectangles 1.5 x 8, centered at X=-14 and X=14, from Z=0 to Z=10
Extrude both -6 in -Y (snap prongs), leaving an inner face-to-face gap of 28.1 between the two prongs

hardware.notes: Glued into the base-plate's underside pockets, flush with the bottom face, to hold the brace to a steel case floor

assembly_steps: Press the riser-tube into the base-plate's top socket until it seats flush; add a drop of plastic-safe adhesive if the fit feels loose
Glue the 4 disc magnets into the base-plate's underside pockets, flush with the surface
Press the TPU friction pad into the gpu-cradle's top trough
Slide the gpu-cradle onto the riser-tube, choose the pin hole that puts the trough level with the GPU's underside, and insert a locking pin through the cradle and that hole
Snap the cable-comb onto the riser-tube at a convenient height and route the PCIe power cable through its slots
Set the base-plate on the case floor beneath the GPU; the magnets hold it to a steel floor, and the cradle should sit just under the card's far edge
